parameters.jsCode: const response=$input.first().json; const body=response.body; if(response.statusCode!==200 || typeof body?.id!=='string' || !/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/i.test(body.id)) return [{json:{valid:false,http_status:response.statusCode===401||response.statusCode===403?401:503,error:'Session verification failed'}}]; const input=$('Validate the intake contract').first().json; return [{json:{valid:true,user_id:body.id,request_id:input.request_id,source_type:input.source_type,content:input.content}}];

const result=$input.first().json; if(typeof result.raw_item_id!=='string') return [{json:{valid:false,http_status:500,error:'Database did not confirm the save'}}]; return [{json:{http_status:result.was_created?201:200,raw_item_id:result.raw_item_id,processing_status:result.processing_status,was_created:result.was_created}}];

parameters.content:
## Ingest — verify → save → confirm → Understand
Ownership comes from Supabase Auth, never the request body. Database writes and activity logging are atomic. Repeated request IDs return the existing item. Confirm the save before starting asynchronous analysis; its queue checker also recovers a missed dispatch. Session data is removed from the child input. Execution data is not retained because the request contains a user session token. Configure the fixed Supabase Auth URL, public API key and Postgres credential.

parameters.query: with saved as materialized (select public.worker_ingest_email($1::text,$2::uuid,$3::text,$4::jsonb) as result), registered as (insert into opportunityos_private.execution_owners(execution_id,user_id,workflow) select $5::text,r.user_id,'01-ingest' from saved s join public.raw_items r on r.id=(s.result->>'raw_item_id')::uuid where (s.result->>'accepted')::boolean on conflict do nothing) select result from saved;
